关键词: Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA)
Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association
主要内容: The Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee (TBAC) convened in a closed session on July 30, 2019, at the Department of the Treasury. Key officials, including Deputy Secretary Justin Muzinich, Director of the Office of Debt Management Fred Pietrangeli, and Federal Reserve Bank of New York staff members, attended the meeting. Pietrangeli provided an overview of the fiscal situation, noting that FY2019 year-to-date receipts totaled $2.6 trillion, or $68 billion (3%) higher than the comparable period last year. Year-to-date outlays totaled $3.4 trillion, or $205 billion (7%) higher than the previous year. He discussed recent borrowing estimates, highlighting the decline in bill issuance due to seasonal factors and the debt limit impasse. The Treasury increased its cash balance target for the end of September to $350 billion following the agreement to suspend the debt limit through July 2021. Pietrangeli also noted the potential impact of the legislation to increase spending caps on future financing needs, emphasizing the need to monitor the Federal Reserve’s balance sheet policy announcements. The TBAC met on July 30, 2019, to discuss Treasury’s financing needs and Federal Reserve policy outlook. Primary dealers indicated that Treasury was well funded for the remainder of the year and did not expect changes to coupon sizes in the current quarter. Some speculated about increasing auction sizes toward the end of FY2020, but there was no consensus on timing. The majority of primary dealers expected the Federal Reserve to cut the federal funds rate by 25 basis points and to end balance sheet normalization early. Debt Manager Katzenbach reviewed Treasury’s cash balance policy, introduced in May 2015, which maintains a minimum cash balance of $150 billion to cover expected outflows. Over the 12-month period ending June 30, 2019, the average minimum cash balance was $232 billion, with the top 20% averaging $365 billion. Primary dealers anticipated an increase in Treasury bill supply of $178 billion over eight weeks following the resolution of the debt ceiling impasse, compared to a market capacity of $210 billion. The Committee discussed the balance between risk management and potential market disruptions from increased bill supply. Deputy Director Steele addressed primary dealers’ views on central clearing for Treasury securities, noting support for expanded clearing and concerns about costs and risk concentration. The Committee emphasized the need for continued feedback and evaluation on these topics. The TBAC of the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA) met on July 30, 2019, to discuss the issuance of Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) and the potential introduction of a 1-year floating rate note (FRN) indexed to the Secured Overnight Finance Rate (SOFR). The Committee recommended a gradual increase in annual TIPS issuance by $20-30 billion in CY2019, with specific reopenings for 30-year, 10-year, and 5-year TIPS. The Committee also suggested the introduction of a 1-year SOFR FRN, citing increased demand for such instruments and the potential to diversify Treasury’s funding costs. However, the Committee acknowledged the potential impact on existing 3-month Treasury bill FRN demand and recommended further study. The meeting concluded with a discussion on market developments and the adjournment of the session. The TBAC convened in a closed session at the Department of the Treasury at 9:15 a.m. on July 30, 2019. The meeting focused on several key topics, including potential changes to Treasury’s coupon auctions. The committee was asked to evaluate the introduction of a 1-year final maturity Floating Rate Note (FRN), specifically comparing a hypothetical 1-year SOFR FRN or 1-year T-bill FRN with an increase in 1-year T-bill issuance. The discussion also included an analysis of how investor demand might vary across these products and an estimation of the relative interest cost and risk to Treasury across the interest rate cycle for these three potential product choices. Additionally, the committee was requested to provide advice on the composition of Treasury notes and bonds to refund approximately $57.3 billion of privately-held notes maturing on August 15, 2019, as well as the composition of marketable financing for the remainder of the July-September 2019 quarter and the October-December 2019 quarter, including cash management bills.
